newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares see smart recovery, index up 2.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares see smart recovery, index up 2.9 pct.

text.p: Bombay's benchmark stocks index surged 2.96 percent on Thursday, propelled by bids from funds and speculators, traders said.
They said prices rose on heavy short covering by punters in Calcutta and Bombay and select bids by foreign and local funds.
Bombay's 30-share stocks index leaped 90.03 points or 2.96 percent to a provisional close of 3127.66.
"Everything was heavily oversold and some correction had to come. Some buying from Indian insitutions has helped to prop up sentiment," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Traders said foreign funds were selective bidders in HDFC, MTNL, BSES, Wartsila Diesel, Bajaj Auto, Hindustan Lever, TELCO, Infosys and BPCL.
Traders said speculators who had long positions during the sharp decline earlier this week were rushing to cover positions after bids by local funds.
Some traders said an auction of around 96,400 ITC shares was likely to take place later today on the National Stock Exchange.
The Calcutta settlement -- which began last Friday -- will continue for a month allowing speculators to keep positions for longer without deliveries.
"The badla (carry forward) charges for this settlement were pretty nominal last Thursday since the market was heavily oversold," one Calcutta trader said.
Analysts said the rise was unlikely to sustain.
"I don't see any immediate reasons for the market to pick up in a hurry," Alok Sethi, director at NatWest Markets in Bombay, said, adding that there may be occasional corrections.
Sethi listed political worries, a slowing growth, weak half year corporate results and commodity stocks as negative factors handicapping the market for the rest of the year.
"The political risk factor is the major constraint on the market today. All the other factors are functions of the political situation," Anthony Duckworth, director of research at W.I Carr said.
